Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
Vulnerabilities.Description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
Vulnerabilities.Description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
Vulnerabilities.Description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: SSH host verification bypass when using schemeless URLs with SFTP/SCP
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When a user invokes curl using a schemeless URL combined with
`--proto-default` sftp (or scp), a disconnect occurs between the tool layer
and libcurl. The tool layer incorrectly infers the URL scheme, which
erroneously bypasses the initialization of critical SSH security options like
CURLOPT_SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 and CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. Conversely, the
libcurl runtime successfully honors CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL and establishes
the connection via SFTP/SCP as specified. Because the tool layer skipped the
security configuration, these SSH host verification options are silently
omitted, causing curl to connect to an unverified SSH remote host without
throwing an error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Unauthorized connection reuse due to a logical error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong connection when asked to
do Negotiate-authenticated ones, even when they are set to use different
"services".

libcurl features a pool of recent connections so that subsequent requests can
reuse an existing connection to avoid overhead.

When reusing a connection a range of criteria must be met. Due to a logical
error in the code, a request that was issued by an application could
wrongfully reuse an existing connection to the same server that was
authenticated using different services.

Vulnerabilities.Title: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the libacl pathname-based functions acl_get_file(), acl_set_file(), acl_extended_file(), and acl_delete_def_file() that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing any pathname component with a symbolic link. Attackers who control any component of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of access control lists and local privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun

Vulnerabilities.Description: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests. Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority

After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: postgresql: PostgreSQL: Privilege escalation via unqualified type resolution in temporary schema

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: postgresql: postgresql: Arbitrary code execution via use-after-free in PL/Perl
Vulnerabilities.Description: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via dropping the final reference to a Perl array or hash while PostgreSQL is converting that object. Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via memory leak in QUIC stream handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted HTTP/2 Server via Rapid Stream Reset
Vulnerabilities.Description:
## Summary

An uncontrolled-resource-consumption vulnerability (CWE-400) in the Twisted HTTP/2 server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server CPU over a single connection. A client that sends a request header block with `END_STREAM` and then immediately resets the stream makes the server route and render the request before it processes the reset. Reset streams are freed and never count against the concurrent-stream limit, and no reset-rate limiter exists, so the pattern can be repeated at line rate on one connection. This is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class, CVE-2023-44487.

## Details

For one received segment the h2 events are processed in order in `H2Connection.dataReceived`. A `HEADERS(END_STREAM)` followed by `RST_STREAM` yields `RequestReceived`, `StreamEnded`, then `StreamReset`, so the request is dispatched and rendered on stream end before the reset is handled:

```python
# src/twisted/web/_http2.py  (H2Connection.dataReceived)
for event in events:
    if isinstance(event, h2.events.RequestReceived):
        self._requestReceived(event)     # allocate the request
    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamEnded):
        self._requestEnded(event)        # -> requestComplete -> render() synchronously
    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamReset):
        self._requestAborted(event)      # processed last, frees the stream
```

`_requestAborted` frees the reset stream, so it never occupies the 100-stream concurrency budget, and nothing in `_http2.py` counts or throttles opened-and-reset streams. The 2019 flood fix (GHSA-32gv) bounds outbound control-frame buffering only and does not apply to this path.

Affected product: Twisted, `twisted.web` HTTP/2 server
Affected versions: confirmed against 26.4.0

## PoC

On any Twisted HTTP/2 endpoint, open one connection and, in a tight loop, send a `HEADERS` frame with `END_STREAM` on a fresh stream identifier immediately followed by a `RST_STREAM` for that stream, at line rate. No credentials are required. The server renders each request on stream end before the reset frees the stream, and a freed stream never counts toward the concurrent-stream limit, so the loop is never throttled.

Because every cancelled stream is still dispatched in full and reset streams do not accumulate, the connection is never throttled or closed, so the forced work grows with the number of pairs sent. Sustained on one connection this saturates a CPU core under only a trickle of traffic, whereas a client that instead leaves its streams open is closed once it reaches the concurrent-stream limit.

## Impact

This is an unauthenticated remote denial of service (CWE-400, CWE-770) by CPU exhaustion. One connection forces unbounded request rendering at a few frames per cancelled request, bypassing the concurrent-stream limit. It is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class (CVE-2023-44487), not covered by the earlier Twisted flood fix, with no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: msgpack: msgpack: Denial of Service via memory leak during map deserialization
Vulnerabilities.Description: MessagePack is the serializer implementation for Python msgpack.org. Prior to 1.2.3, the msgpack-python C extension (msgpack._cmsgpack) leaks a decoded map value when deserialization rejects a key with strict_map_key=True (the default). Repeated malformed inputs can cause unbounded process memory growth and denial of service in applications that deserialize attacker-controlled MessagePack data. Both unpackb() and the streaming Unpacker API are affected. The pure-Python fallback does not exhibit this leak in the reported tests. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.3.

Vulnerabilities.Title: MessagePack for Python: Out-of-bounds read / crash on Unpacker reuse after a caught error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
### Impact

If the Unpacker is used repeatedly after an error occurs, the process may crash with a SEGV.

If the Unpacker is used repeatedly to unpack untrusted input from external sources, it may be vulnerable to a DoS attack.

### Patches

v1.2.1

### Workarounds

Users should create a new Unpacker instead of reusing the same Unpacker after an error occurs.

Applying the above patch can prevent SEGV, but reusing the Streaming Unpacker after it has encountered an error will not yield correct data. If an error occurs during Streaming Unpacking, the Stream and Streaming Unpacker should be discarded.

Therefore, this is not just a workaround but the correct solution. The above patch only prevents crashes from incorrect usage.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pyasn1: pyasn1: Denial of Service via hash collisions in schemaless decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. From 0.3.3 until 0.6.5, schemaless container decoding stores every decoded component's TagSet in a growing set even though only one-versus-multiple tag types must be distinguished. Attacker-controlled BER, CER, or DER input contains many distinct long tag IDs whose TagSet hashes collide. Each later set insertion compares against an increasing number of earlier colliding tags in ConstructedPayloadDecoderBase._decodeComponentsSchemaless, producing quadratic CPU work while decoded values and order remain valid. Repeated inputs can exhaust decoder CPU and reduce service availability. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pyasn1: pyasn1: Denial of Service via quadratic processing of fragmented ASN.1 data
Vulnerabilities.Description: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding repeatedly concatenates each fragment onto a growing bytes value. Attacker-controlled BER or CER data can use many constructed OCTET STRING or character-string fragments. DER rejects constructed OCTET STRING without a schema, but accepts its definite-length form when asn1Spec selects univ.OctetString; it also accepts constructed character strings such as UTF8String without a schema, even though those encodings are not valid DER. The separate indefinite-length ANY path is reachable in BER and CER when asn1Spec selects univ.Any; DER rejects indefinite lengths. OctetStringPayloadDecoder uses growing header concatenation and AnyPayloadDecoder.indefLenValueDecoder uses growing chunk concatenation, repeatedly copying an increasing prefix and causing quadratic work. A sufficiently fragmented value can occupy decoding workers and cause CPU exhaustion without confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pyasn1: pyasn1: Denial of Service via constructed bit string decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, constructed BIT STRING decoding repeatedly shifts and copies the complete bit value accumulated from earlier fragments. Attacker-controlled BER or CER input contains many constructed BIT STRING fragments; schema-driven DER also accepts a definite-length constructed BIT STRING. BitStringPayloadDecoder repeatedly calls BitString.fromOctetString with the prior bitString as prepend, shifting an ever-growing SizedInteger for each fragment and causing quadratic work. Large fragmented values can exhaust CPU during decode() without requiring later conversion or formatting. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pyasn1: pyasn1: Denial of Service via quadratic complexity in binary REAL decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: pyasn1 is a generic ASN.1 library for Python. Prior to 0.6.5, binary REAL decoding builds a large mantissa one octet at a time by shifting a growing integer and slicing the remaining byte string. Attacker-controlled ASN.1 includes a binary-encoded REAL with a large mantissa and reaches BER, CER, or DER decode(), with or without a schema containing REAL. RealPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder repeatedly performs a left shift, OR, and suffix copy for every mantissa octet, making decode time quadratic in mantissa length. A comparatively small REAL value can hold a decoding worker on one CPU core for seconds or longer and cause availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.5.

Vulnerabilities.Title: setuptools: Path Traversal Vulnerability in setuptools PackageIndex

Version 78.1.1 fixes the issue.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautifu ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 4.0, Soup Sieve repeatedly walks the same ancestors while matching descendant combinators, and each additional descendant combinator raises the polynomial degree of the work on deeply nested attacker-influenced HTML or XML. Applications using selectors such as section div div through select(), select_one(), or Beautiful Soup CSS APIs against untrusted documents can have a worker occupied for seconds or minutes, while trusted-only document processing is not affected. Selectors compiled with NOCACHE continue to use the old uncached behavior. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautifu ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 3.0, the CSS_ESCAPES and IDENTIFIER regular-expression subpatterns can backtrack exponentially on runs of ambiguous digit escapes in an attribute-name or tag position of an otherwise valid selector. The failure occurs during selector compilation through soupsieve.compile() or Beautiful Soup select() before SELECTOR_LIMIT is applied, so an application that accepts untrusted selector strings can have a worker stalled by a short input. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: urllib3: urllib3: Traffic interception via HTTPS proxy TLS configuration override
Vulnerabilities.Description: urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. From 1.26.0 until 2.8.0, the proxy_ssl_context, proxy_assert_hostname, proxy_assert_fingerprint, ssl_context, cert_reqs, verify_mode, use_forwarding_for_https=True, and CERT_NONE configuration paths fail to remain separated because target-server TLS settings are incorrectly applied to the HTTPS proxy connection. The trigger is that an application uses an HTTPS proxy and configures target-server TLS settings that must remain separate from the proxy TLS handshake, including HTTPS forwarding with target-specific identity or credentials. Applying cert_reqs=CERT_NONE can overwrite proxy_ssl_context.verify_mode in place, and the mutation persists so later connections reusing the same context may connect to the HTTPS proxy without certificate verification. The attack mechanism is that an attacker intercepts and impersonates the HTTPS proxy after the effective proxy policy accepts the attacker's certificate. The impact is that the attacker can observe or modify forwarded traffic or receive a target TLS client certificate, while CONNECT tunneling still preserves the separate end-to-end target TLS connection. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: urllib3: urllib3: Denial of Service via unbounded memory allocation in chunk parser
Vulnerabilities.Description: urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. From 1.10.3 until 2.8.0, the HTTPResponse.read_chunked and HTTPResponse.stream methods can allocate unbounded memory because the streaming chunk parser buffers the chunk-size field until newline or EOF without a length bound. The trigger is that a malicious server returns Transfer-Encoding: chunked followed by a very long run of bytes without a newline. The attack mechanism is that a malicious HTTP server sends a very long unterminated chunk-size line. The impact is that unbounded memory allocation can exhaust the client process. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption
Vulnerabilities.Description: During session resumption in crypto/tls, if the underlying Config has its ClientCAs or RootCAs fields mutated between the initial handshake and the resumed handshake, the resumed handshake may succeed when it should have failed. This may happen when a user calls Config.Clone and mutates the returned Config, or uses Config.GetConfigForClient. This can cause a client to resume a session with a server that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake, or cause a server to resume a session with a client that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: net/url: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
Vulnerabilities.Description: The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: Denial of Service due to excessive resource consumption via crafted certificate
Vulnerabilities.Description: Within HostnameError.Error(), when constructing an error string, there is no limit to the number of hosts that will be printed out. Furthermore, the error string is constructed by repeated string concatenation, leading to quadratic runtime. Therefore, a certificate provided by a malicious actor can result in excessive resource consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
Vulnerabilities.Description: On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action. To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/url: Incorrect parsing of IPv6 host literals in net/url
Vulnerabilities.Description: url.Parse insufficiently validated the host/authority component and accepted some invalid URLs.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
Vulnerabilities.Description: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building
Vulnerabilities.Description: During chain building, the amount of work that is done is not correctly limited when a large number of intermediate certificates are passed in VerifyOptions.Intermediates, which can lead to a denial of service. This affects both direct users of crypto/x509 and users of crypto/tls.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/x509: golang: Go crypto/x509: Denial of Service via inefficient certificate chain validation
Vulnerabilities.Description: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via long CNAME response in LookupCNAME
Vulnerabilities.Description: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net: Go HTTP/2: Denial of Service via malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE frame
Vulnerabilities.Description: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
Vulnerabilities.Description: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/mail: golang: Go net/mail: Denial of Service via crafted email inputs
Vulnerabilities.Description: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
Vulnerabilities.Description: The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
Vulnerabilities.Description: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the a path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, 'root.Open("symlink/")' will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via NUL byte in Dial and LookupPort on Windows
Vulnerabilities.Description: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/mail: golang: net/mail: Denial of Service via pathological email address parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
Vulnerabilities.Description: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
Vulnerabilities.Description: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.

Vulnerabilities.Title: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, pathological inputs could close an unescaped '/' early, allowing for attack-controlled data to inject arbitrary content, potentially leading to XSS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, DecodeElement would reset the depth counter causing it to never fire; this could lead to stack exhaustion.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
Vulnerabilities.Description: Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead. Now, path resolution operates on a byte buffer using index-based backtracking for '..' segments, eliminating the quadratic time complexity and significantly reducing memory allocations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
Vulnerabilities.Description: When parsing a Range header containing a large number of small ranges, FileServer(FS), ServeContent, and ServeFile(FS) can consume an excessive amount of CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
Vulnerabilities.Description: A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in the client or server by opening a large number of streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values.

Vulnerabilities.Title: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
Vulnerabilities.Description: Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in the server process by specifying multiple references. We now reject these as malformed and curb the memory amplification vector as a result.
